kind: A screen by slope over data on the test bed, one seed on the laptop and two on the server, and a pilot at full size of 24,000 updates, one seed, which the laptop's seed can stop.
why: The census by rate (unit_density_by_rate.json) found that the stack's silent cells sink. At the rates where the stack trains best, 63% to 86% of cells and bytes at full size stand more than eight whole thresholds below zero charge, and 1% to 3.5% within one threshold below firing; on the test bed at 1.2e-3 it is 35% after 6,000 updates and 57% after 24,000. The code thins with the rate and with data (nine tenths of a level's spikes come from 11% of its cells at 6e-4 and from 4% at 1.2e-3, where half of the Transformer's units carry nine tenths at every rate), and the stack stops gaining from the rate where its code is thin. A plain cell learns from a smooth threshold that is one fine spike wide, a sixteenth of a whole threshold: its slope is zero from a fifth of a threshold below zero on. So a cell learns at a byte only where it fires or almost fires. Nothing tells a silent cell that its spikes are wanted at a byte, and nothing holds its charge at the bytes where it is silent: that charge drifts with every change that the bytes where it fires ask of its synapses. The roadmap's eighth bet says what a remedy needs: it has to reach several thresholds below the rest. What was tried does not reach. Noisy thresholds, half a threshold wide, were level (noisy_thresholds_with_data.json). A smooth threshold a whole threshold wide was 0.0145 behind at full size after 6,000 updates at 1e-3 and 0.074 behind after 15,000 (docs/STREAM_FORM_ARMS.md, fp16-wide0-1e-3 and fp16-wide-1e-3): that slope dies within three thresholds, it is negative from 0.75 to 3 thresholds below zero, where it tells a cell to fall further when more of its spikes are wanted, and it halves the slope of a cell that has just begun to fire. In a neuron, plasticity does not wait for a spike: a synapse changes when its input meets a depolarised membrane, by how far the membrane stands from its threshold (voltage-dependent plasticity; Artola, Broecher and Singer 1990; Clopath, Buesing, Vasilaki and Gerstner 2010). The slope built here (b422510, --granule-slope-tail T) follows that: the cell's spikes are unchanged, its slope is one for charge above zero, as it is for the spikes that the cell fires, and 1 / (1 + d / T)^2 at d whole thresholds below zero, a power law, so a cell 8 thresholds below still learns at a ninth for T = 4, where the smooth threshold's slope is zero to fifteen places. It comes in two forms. In the first the slope below zero teaches everything that the charge depends on: the cell's synapses and rest, the stream that it hears and the pool. In the second (--granule-slope-tail-local) it teaches only the cell's own synapses and its rest, and the stream and the pool learn from charge above zero alone: a rule of three factors, the input's spikes, the membrane's distance from its threshold and the error that the cell's output synapses bring back, which never tells the rest of the network about spikes that were not fired. A slope where a cell did not fire is a guess and not the slope of what the network computes; the second form keeps that guess inside the cell. The cost: no pulse and no parameter; the second form sums every cell's charge twice while training.

arms.tail-local: --granule-slope-tail 4 --granule-slope-tail-local: the same slope, teaching only the cell's own synapses and rest; the same parameters

measure: experiments/eval_stream.py on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 lead bytes, averaged weights, bits of every piece kept; each arm paired with the base of its seed and length; experiments/gap_by_piece.py splits each lead by what the context offers (near 240 on the bed and 496 at full size, far 8,192). Beside the bits: the trainer's pulses a byte and its time for 1,500 updates, and on the laptop's seed and at full size the census that found the sinking cells (experiments/cell_activity.py on the trained weights: the cells that fire at a byte, the cells that send nine tenths of a level's spikes, and the cells and bytes by charge in thresholds).
reading: The bed. The server's two seeds are read by experiments/read_lead_study.py's shared reading, each form by itself: a form is a fix for late learning if at 24,000 updates its mean lead over the base is at least 0.010 with both seeds ahead and its mean lead at 24,000 updates is at least 0.005 larger than at 6,000; a lead at 24,000 without that growth is a constant gain; anything else fails on the bed. The laptop's seed is reported as a third seed and does one more thing, because it is scored before the server's window opens: a form that is 0.010 or more behind its base at 24,000 updates there is not run at full size. For a form with both of the server's seeds ahead at 24,000 updates, the depths 1 and 16 run on the server's two seeds at 24,000 updates and are reported. Full size. One seed: these readings direct what is built next. A form's gain is fs-st6 minus its arm at 6e-4. A gain of at least 0.010 earns the form a place in the next full-size stack, tried first in a pilot of that stack written before it runs; with two forms there the one with the larger gain takes it, and at less than 0.003 between them the local one, which guesses less. A gain from 0.005 up to 0.010 is a small gain and is tested again only inside such a pilot; less is reported only, and the bed does not overrule it. The rate: a form lifts the stack's rate if its arm at 1.2e-3 scores at least 0.005 below its arm at 6e-4, as the Transformer's does (0.0074); then the next full-size stack trains at 1.2e-3. What the mechanism itself predicts is read as well and decides nothing: with the slope, fewer cells and bytes stand more than eight thresholds below zero than in the base (57% on the laptop's seed after 24,000 updates, 63% at full size at 6e-4 and 86% at 1.2e-3), and more cells carry nine tenths of a level's spikes. If the bits improve and the census does not move, the slope works some other way than the one written here, and the report says so. Recorded either way: every lead, the leads on new contexts, the pulses a byte, the time, and the census.
seen_before_recording: No arm has trained to a score. Stress runs of 120 updates on the laptop's CPU (peak rate 1.2e-3 reached after 30 updates, seed 20003, not a measure): on the trainer's windows and on streams the base reads 3.3026 and 3.2600 after 120 updates, tail 3.3630 and 3.3059, tail-local 3.3781 and 3.3187, so both forms start a little slower; an update takes 0.87, 0.88 and 0.91 seconds. The base trains bit for bit as on the copy of 4ddd867 (the same 120 updates, compared line by line). One backward pass on the laptop's trained base (rd-base-24k-s3, 8 windows of 256 validation bytes): under tail the gradient of the cells' input synapses is 1.36 times as large as under the smooth threshold and has a cosine of 0.84 with it, and the gradient of everything else is 1.14 times as large with a cosine of 0.95; under tail-local it is 1.17 times and 0.89 for the cells' synapses, and 0.99 times and 0.998 for everything else. The census and the two wide slopes as cited above. The full-size pair's Transformer has scored 1.0790 on the test split; its stack is still training.
